messages:
Lena (Product): Usability + localization note: customers in EMEA reported the probe details are unreadable in German and Arabic locales because the status labels are too long and the layout doesn't handle RTL. We need a plan.
Omar (Design): Interesting. Two UX problems: (1) labels overflow on small screens for long translations (German tends to expand), (2) RTL flips make the timestamp alignment confusing. Proposal: introduce compact status tokens (OK / Check / No resp) mapping to localized long-form copy only on hover/expand.
Priya (Eng): Backend can emit a compact status code `p_ok | p_warn | p_fail` and an optional `verbose_label` for the UI to show on expand. That keeps transport small and lets translators control long forms.
Diego (Frontend): Implementation detail: render compact token (one short word) in the main row and expose full localized text in the expanded details and tooltip. For RTL support, mirror the layout and put the timestamp at the start of the row (visually), but keep the DOM order consistent for screen readers.
IntlBot: Localization guidance: prefer shorter source strings for keys that will be shown inline. Provide context comments for translators explaining UI constraints. Suggest length caps: 18 characters for inline tokens, 80 for detail lines. Link: https://i18n.example/guidelines#short-strings
A11yBot: Accessibility: when switching to RTL visually, ensure focus order remains logical. Use dir="auto" on localized elements and provide clear aria-labels for compact tokens like aria-label="SSH check: No response from host". Avoid injecting text via CSS pseudo-elements for screen readers.
Lena (Product): Copy decisions: compact tokens should be human-readable: suggestions: 'Checking' -> 'Checking', 'Success' -> 'Ok', 'Timeout' -> 'No resp'. For translations, use glossary entries. Also add a short helper above probes: 'Short labels used for compact view 1 to avoid truncation; expand for details.'
Omar (Design): Visual: add a tiny info icon next to the compact token that opens a tooltip. For touch devices, long-press reveals details. Also add subtle divider rules when view is RTL so groups don't visually merge.
Diego (Frontend): We'll add keyboard support: focusable info icon with Enter/Space to open tooltip, Escape to close. Also allow pressing 'D' when focused on the probe list to download a debug bundle for current run. Is that OK?
Priya (Eng): We can generate a small debug bundle with probe logs and timestamps and a short anonymized fingerprint. Backend will expose an endpoint `/debug-bundle?run_id=...` that returns a gzipped JSON. We'll also emit a `debug_code` like `DBG-2026-9A3` which can be copied into support tickets.
Lena (Product): Love the debug code idea. For privacy, ensure the bundle excludes customer payloads and IPs by default. Add a checkbox 'Include network traces' when advanced. Also add a small one-line tooltip copy: 'Download debug bundle to share with Support.'
IntlBot: Note for translators: include placeholder for debug code format. Some languages need different ordering, so keep tokenized strings minimal.
A11yBot: Also ensure the debug download control is reachable by screen reader users and announces the debug code after generation (aria-live polite). Provide a copy button next to the code.
OpsBot: Telemetry: emit `debug_bundle_generated` with hashed_run_id and `include_traces: true|false`. Limit generation to 5 per account per hour to prevent abuse.
Diego (Frontend): Will prototype compact tokens + info icon + keyboard shortcut + debug bundle UI in Figma and add a small RTL demo. Posting link here by Tue EOD.
Priya (Eng): I'll add the `compact_status` field and `debug_code` to the probe run schema in branch `compact-i18n-debug`. Also will implement privacy filters on the bundle.
Omar (Design): Action items: update visuals for RTL, add info icon microcopy, define compact token set. Lena to create glossary entries for translators. IntlBot & A11yBot to review. Target next sprint.
Lena (Product): Thanks team 1 this should make the wizard friendlier internationally and speed up support workflows.
